name: Auto Story Generator - 9 Genres
description: Creates a fresh original US English story from genre settings only, with continuity controls and episode packaging.

steps.name: 1. Research brief
template: You are a senior story development researcher for US audio storytelling aimed at listeners age {{input.auto_age_segment}}.
The user will not provide a topic. Build a practical inspiration brief for a NEW original story.
Required setting lane for this run, if provided: {{input.auto_setting_prompt}}

If a required setting lane is provided, treat it as the story spine, not a rigid checklist. Keep the same broad family-drama situation and emotional betrayal, but you may change names, exact objects, jobs, location, family roles, and evidence details if that makes the story more natural. Do not switch to a totally different lane.
Use public-domain and lawful reference areas only as inspiration for structure, motifs, and atmosphere. Do not copy any protected text, plot, named fictional character, or modern article.

Useful reference areas: Project Gutenberg public-domain fiction shelves, LibriVox public-domain audiobooks, Library of Congress Chronicling America historic newspapers, Internet Archive old-time radio/audio drama, folklore and public-domain archetypes.
Important: If the genre is True Crime, default to FICTIONAL true-crime style unless verifiable public-domain historical material is clearly used. Do not invent accusations about real living people.
Previous Auto Story history for this genre. Avoid repeating these titles, premises, settings, jobs, victim/offender dynamics, and core twists:
Return a concise research brief with:
- 8 fresh natural variations around the required setting lane if one is provided; otherwise 8 fresh premise lanes that avoid the history above
- retention devices for the first 5 minutes
- best lane to use today and why

steps.name: 2. Story concept
template: Create ONE fresh original story concept from the research brief.
- Do not use the same title, premise, setting, profession mix, or core twist from the previous history.
- The story must be logically causal: every major reveal must be planted earlier.
- Keep the premise grounded and emotionally clear for audio.
- If True Crime, make it fictional true-crime style unless explicitly framed as public-domain historical inspiration.
Required setting lane for this run, if provided: {{input.auto_setting_prompt}}

If a required setting lane is provided, use it as the core direction but do not force every detail literally. The concept should feel like an organic story, not a checklist. Do not switch to a totally different lane or default to a store/business/property-sale premise unless the lane points that way.
Why this is not a repeat:

steps.name: 3. Continuity bible
template: Build a strict continuity bible for the story concept below.
The bible exists to prevent random, unrelated, or contradictory chapters.
Every later chapter must obey it.
CHARACTERS: names, ages, roles, motives, secrets, voice notes.
SETTING: location, time period, social world, sensory palette.
TIMELINE: chronological truth of what happened before chapter 1 and during the episode.
EVIDENCE / OBJECTS / PROMISES: important clues, proof objects, vows, debts, letters, recordings, records, or artifacts.
CAUSE AND EFFECT RULES: what must cause what.
FORBIDDEN CONTRADICTIONS: things the script must never violate.
ENDING PAYOFF CHECKLIST: questions that must be answered by the end.

steps.name: 4. Beat outline
template: Create a beat-by-beat outline for a {{input.expected_duration}} audio story.
10-50%: investigation, relationship build, complications, or practical steps depending on genre.
50-90%: reversals, escalation, proof, confession, confrontation, or transformation.
90-100%: payoff, emotional resolution, and teaser/open loop if appropriate.
Return only the beat outline. Each beat must include: purpose, key event, clue/turning point, emotional shift, and logic note.

steps.name: 5. Character bible
template: Create a compact visual character bible for image/video generation.
- Each line must start with the exact full character name, followed by a comma, then age, face, hair, build, wardrobe palette, role, and emotional presence.
- Include only recurring or visually important characters.
- Use realistic American casting details. No markdown, no headings.

steps.name: 6. Chapter plan
template: Split the story into exactly {{chapter.count}} chapters for voice narration.
- continuity facts that must be preserved

steps.name: 7. Metadata + SFX cues
template: Create an episode package as valid JSON only. No markdown.
SFX cues are instructions only; do not claim audio files were generated.

steps.name: 8. Chapter 01
template: Write Chapter 1 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only the narration text. No title, no chapter label, no bullets, no markdown, no production notes, no SFX labels.
Start with the planned hook within the first 60 words. Use dialogue naturally, but do not write speaker labels.

steps.name: 9. Chapter 02
template: Write Chapter 2 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only narration. No labels, bullets, markdown, notes, or SFX.
Continue causally from Chapter 1 and preserve all facts.

steps.name: 10. Chapter 03
template: Write Chapter 3 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only narration. No labels, bullets, markdown, notes, or SFX.
Escalate the central conflict and plant the next reveal.

steps.name: 11. Chapter 04
template: Write Chapter 4 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only narration. No labels, bullets, markdown, notes, or SFX.
Use the continuity bible to make the reversal feel earned, not random.

steps.name: 12. Chapter 05
template: Write Chapter 5 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only narration. No labels, bullets, markdown, notes, or SFX.
If this is the final selected chapter count, resolve the main promise while leaving a light teaser. If more chapters are planned, end with a strong open loop.

steps.name: 13. Chapter 06
template: Write Chapter 6 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only narration. No labels, bullets, markdown, notes, or SFX.
If this is the final selected chapter count, deliver the ending payoff and answer the promised questions.

steps.name: 14. Chapter 07
template: Write Chapter 7 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only narration. No labels, bullets, markdown, notes, or SFX.
Move into the final confrontation or final transformation.

steps.name: 15. Chapter 08
template: Write Chapter 8 as finished voice-ready narration in American English.
Return only narration. No labels, bullets, markdown, notes, or SFX.
Resolve the main promise, pay off planted clues, and end with a satisfying final emotional note.
